h1: How to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets
answer: Use Shopify Flow's "Add row to spreadsheet" action or an automation that adds a row on each new order.
Decide one row per order or per item first, and catch cancellations, which a new-order trigger never sees.

root.q: How often do you need the orders in a sheet?

then.why: Orders, Export. Up to 50 orders download at once; bigger exports are emailed to you. Extra line items already sit on their own rows.

then.q: What will you do with the sheet?

then.why: Order number, date, customer, items joined in one cell, total. SUM the total column. In Flow, one Add row action.
Repeat the order number on each item row. Sum line prices, never the order total. In Flow, wrap Add row in For each.

method.h2: How to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets

steps.title: Build the header row
steps.body: Order number first, then date, customer, the columns for your choice above, and a Status column. Freeze the header.

steps.title: Pick the trigger on purpose
steps.body: New order catches every order, paid or not; order paid catches only money in. In viaSocket's catalog Shopify has "New Order", "Order Paid" and "Order Cancelled" triggers.

steps.title: Map line items deliberately
steps.body: One row per order: join items in one cell ("2 x Oat Latte Blend, 1 x Grinder"). One row per item: loop over the line items and repeat the order number.

steps.title: Clean the text
steps.body: Strip commas and line breaks from product names and notes, or quote them, so columns stay in place. In Flow, Shopify suggests a Liquid replace filter.

note.text: Flow writes row contents comma-separated, so one comma in a product name shifts every column after it.

steps.title: Catch cancellations
steps.body: A second automation on "Order Cancelled" finds the order number in the sheet and sets Status to Cancelled. Do the same for refunds if you report on them.

steps.title: Test with a real order
steps.body: Place a test order with two products, one with a comma in its name, then cancel it. You should see one or two rows, then a Cancelled status.

captain.line: Captain reads a real order from your store to plan the columns, tests the steps on it, and keeps the automation as a draft until you make it live.

wrong.title: Edited orders leave old numbers
wrong.body: Items and quantities can change after an order is placed, and a new-order trigger never sees it. Add an update step, or reconcile from Shopify monthly.

wrong.title: Duplicate rows
wrong.body: Shopify retries webhooks up to 8 times over 4 hours when an endpoint does not answer within 5 seconds. Look the order number up before adding.

wrong.title: Only paid orders arrived
wrong.body: You picked "order paid" but wanted cash-on-delivery orders too. Switch to new order and keep a Status column.

wrong.title: The sheet slows down
wrong.body: Google Sheets holds up to 20 million cells, but a sheet full of formulas slows far sooner. Start a new tab each year.

faqs.q: Can Shopify export orders straight to Google Sheets?
faqs.a: Not live from the Orders page, which exports CSV files. Shopify Flow's "Add row to spreadsheet" action can write each order into a Google Sheet as it arrives.
Yes, on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus. Its "Send HTTP request" action needs Grow or above, but adding sheet rows does not.

faqs.q: How do I get one row per product?
faqs.a: Loop over the order's line items and add a row for each, repeating the order number. In Flow that is the For each step around Add row.
